residencyRequirements.description: If both parties are New Hampshire residents, there is no minimum residency period. If one party is a non-resident, the filing spouse must have lived in New Hampshire for at least one year before filing.

waitingPeriod.description: New Hampshire has no mandatory waiting period after filing for divorce.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences which have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Extreme Cruelty
fault.description: Extreme cruelty of either party to the other

fault.name: Conviction of a Crime
fault.description: Conviction of a crime punishable by imprisonment for more than one year, if actually sentenced to imprisonment

fault.name: Absence for Two Years
fault.description: Absence of either party for two years without the other's consent and without the other knowing the absent party's whereabouts

fault.name: Habitual Drunkenness
fault.description: Habitual drunkenness for a period of two years

fault.name: Treatment Endangering Health or Reason
fault.description: Treatment that seriously injures health or endangers reason

fault.name: Joining Religious Sect Against Marriage
fault.description: Joining a religious sect or society that professes to believe the relation of husband and wife void, and refusal to cohabit for six months

groundsForDissolution.notes: New Hampshire has both fault and no-fault grounds. The most common ground is irreconcilable differences (no-fault). New Hampshire uniquely includes joining a religious sect that believes marriage is void as a fault ground.

propertyDivision.description: New Hampshire courts divide all property — including both marital and separate property — equitably. The court considers factors including the length of the marriage, the age and health of each party, the amount and sources of income, the occupation and employability of each party, and the contribution of each spouse to the acquisition, preservation, or appreciation of property.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: New Hampshire does not distinguish between marital and separate property. ALL property owned by either or both spouses, however acquired, is subject to equitable distribution.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirements — both residents: no minimum; one non-resident: 1 year
Property division — equitable distribution of all property
Parental Rights and Responsibilities — custody and parenting time

filingFees.notes: As of July 1, 2025, New Hampshire filing fees are $280 for a divorce without minor children and $400 for a divorce with minor children (Circuit Court, Family Division). Fee waivers may be available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Vital Statistics Form
basic.description: Required statistical information for the state

basic.name: Financial Affidavit
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, expenses, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Required plan for parental rights and responsibilities per RSA 461-A

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per New Hampshire Child Support Guidelines (RSA 458-C)

withChildren.name: Uniform Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Rules of the Circuit Court of the State of New Hampshire, Family Division

inState.description: Respondent must file an appearance within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside New Hampshire has 30 days to file an appearance

childSupportGuidelines.description: New Hampshire uses an income shares model. Both parents' adjusted gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the New Hampshire Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined net income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if strict application would be unjust or inappropriate. Self-support reserve applies.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: New Hampshire courts may award alimony after considering factors including the length of the marriage, the age and health of each party, the occupation and sources of income, vocational skills and employability, the property division, and the ability of each party to be self-supporting.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Available based on need and ability to pay. No formula-based calculation.

court.name: Circuit Court, Family Division
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the Circuit Court, Family Division for the county where either party resides. (RSA 490-D)
